subject: Operational availability baseline & monthly compensation ceiling — template edits requested
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Smith <ops@clarityai.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational availability baseline & monthly compensation ceiling — template edits requested

Hi Oliver —

Following our discovery last week, attaching the SLA template we usually start with for customers of this size (redwood_sla_template_v3.docx). Two points we've been asked to lock down before legal kicks off the redline:

1) Availability baseline: our standard is 99.95% monthly across the hosted service. For customers running mixed throughput inference we can consider a slightly different floor — I wanted to surface whether ClarityAI expects anything different.

2) Monthly compensation ceiling: instead of an open-ended credit schedule, we propose a hard cap to simplify procurement: either 10% of monthly invoice or $25,000 (whichever is lower). That keeps your exposure predictable and allows us to offer the SLA without additional underwriting.

If you want different language for scheduled maintenance carve-outs or a regional split, let us know — we've got a couple of optional clauses we can toggle.

Can you share your procurement contact and any initial redlines? If you prefer, we can put a straw-man compromise on the baseline/ceiling and circulate for comment.

Thanks —

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

Attachment: redwood_sla_template_v3.docx (SLA template, editable)
From: Oliver Smith <ops@clarityai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clarityai.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational availability baseline & monthly compensation ceiling — template edits requested

Thanks, Sergio. Quick thoughts from ops and procurement side:

- Availability: 99.95% is ambitious and we appreciate it, but for mission-critical inference we need the option to require 99.99% for specific endpoints (we'll flag which ones). Can the template support endpoint-level baselines?

- Compensation ceiling: the flat 10% / $25k cap is straightforward, but procurement prefers a higher cap tied to a percentage of committed spend — we were thinking 15% of monthly committed spend or $75,000 (whichever is lower).

- Maintenance carve-outs: we'll need a clear definition of scheduled maintenance window and a maximum monthly maintenance budget.

I've attached our first-pass comments to the SLA (clarityai_sla_comments.pdf). I've looped in procurement; they will follow up with commercial redlines.

Oliver
Oliver Smith
Head of Infrastructure, ClarityAI
ops@clarityai.com
Attachment: clarityai_sla_comments.pdf (annotated comments)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Smith <ops@clarityai.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational availability baseline & monthly compensation ceiling — template edits requested

Oliver —

Appreciate the quick read and the attachment. A couple of pragmatic options from our side that might get us to a clean commercial handoff to legal without a full underwriting cycle:

Option A (conservative compromise):
- Default availability baseline: 99.95% for platform-wide endpoints, with the ability to request endpoint-level uplift to 99.99% for designated endpoints (separate addendum + additional reserved capacity billing).
- Monthly compensation ceiling: 12% of monthly committed spend capped at $50,000. This gives ClarityAI a higher ceiling while keeping a concrete cap for our finance team.
- Scheduled maintenance: define a rolling monthly maintenance allowance of up to 6 hours per region (excluded from uptime calculations) with a 30-day advance notice expectation for non-emergency windows.

Option B (short-term pilot):
- Start with 99.95% baseline + 10% cap / $25k for the first 3 months while we observe traffic profile; if SLAs are met consistently we auto-transition to Option A thresholds on month 4.

Practical asks for procurement: please confirm committed monthly spend band so we can calculate the exact dollar cap under Option A. I've summarized these as redlines in the attached doc (I captured some of your notes inline).

If those look OK, I'll draft a one-page summary we can hand to legal and procurement to speed the DocuSign loop.

Thanks —

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success (SaaS & Enterprise), Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

On quick note: Marissa — can you confirm operational feasibility of the endpoint-level uplift and what the additional reserved capacity pricing would look like?
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Smith <ops@clarityai.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, procurement@clarityai.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational availability baseline & monthly compensation ceiling — template edits requested

Oliver / procurement team —

Thanks for the comments and the attachment. To summarize the path forward we've agreed internally as the cleanest negotiation posture:

- Baseline: keep platform-wide default at 99.95%. Add an optional endpoint uplift to 99.99% that requires a short addendum and reserved capacity commitment (Laura will provide estimated uplift pricing).
- Monthly compensation ceiling: propose 12% of committed monthly spend capped at $50,000 (Option A). If procurement prefers a timeboxed pilot, we're open to Option B (3-month pilot at 10% / $25k) with an automatic review.
- Maintenance carve-outs: scheduled maintenance up to 6 hours per region per month excluded; emergency maintenance and security patches to be coordinated with 24-hour notice where possible.

Next steps: Oliver / procurement — confirm which path you prefer (Option A or Option B) and share the committed spend band for the account so we can calculate the dollar cap. Once you confirm, I'll (a) update the SLA template with the agreed language, (b) share a one-page commercial summary, and (c) open the DocuSign envelope for signature.
